summary: Troxerutin is a semisynthetic hydroxyethylrutoside (a derivative of the bioflavonoid rutin) used as a venoactive/phlebotonic agent for chronic venous insufficiency and associated symptoms such as leg heaviness, pain, swelling, night cramps, and varicose-vein-related complaints, as well as for hemorrhoids and capillary fragility. It reduces capillary permeability and fragility and improves venous tone and microcirculation. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on European/SmPC and BNF-type references. It is generally well tolerated, mainly causing mild gastrointestinal effects.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of chronic venous insufficiency (leg heaviness, pain, swelling, cramps)
Symptoms associated with varicose veins and venous disorders
Conditions associated with increased capillary fragility/permeability

moa: Troxerutin is a hydroxyethyl derivative of rutin that acts on the microvasculature to decrease capillary permeability and fragility and to improve venous tone and red-cell flexibility. By stabilizing the capillary endothelium and reducing inflammatory and oxidative changes, it improves microcirculation and reduces edema and symptoms of venous insufficiency.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to troxerutin, rutosides, or formulation components

preg: Use is generally avoided during the first trimester of pregnancy. In later pregnancy use only if clearly necessary and as advised by a clinician, since data are limited.
lact: There are limited data on excretion in breast milk; avoid use during breastfeeding unless considered necessary.

pearls: Not FDA-approved; an established European/Indian venoactive (phlebotonic) flavonoid - this record reflects SmPC/BNF-type labeling
A hydroxyethylrutoside derived from rutin; reduces capillary fragility and improves venous tone
Symptomatic therapy for chronic venous insufficiency - best combined with compression and lifestyle measures
Generally well tolerated, with mild GI effects predominating
Available orally and as a topical gel in some markets
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Excess may cause gastrointestinal upset. Management is supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote. Contact a poison control center for guidance.
